text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The attorney-general has called for a review of tender procedures and Tender Board practices, after criticism of government tendering.

- A crisis over salary increases has once again flared up at the state Namibian Broadcasting Corp, with union members rejecting an across the board eight percent increase offer. Negotiations are continuing.
- Namibia has drawn up a national policy to combat corruption and draft legislation is to be presented to parliament in the next year.

- Commercial farmers are still reeling from last year's drought and have been dealt a further blow by the disappearance of N$4 million earmarked for drought relief. Drought aid promised to farmers for restocking has also been reduced.
- With the demise of South African bottler New Age Beverages, the days of Pepsi in southern Africa appear to be numbered.

- The Development Fund of Namibia is entering the area of small and medium enterprise development. The fund has designed a five-year plan based on the investment of its available capital, and will allocate N$15 million a year over the next five years to develop small- and medium-size businesses.
